source_note: Curated from AARP, Cleveland Clinic, Kaiser Permanente, and NIA-style geriatric guidance. Low-intensity, knee-aware. MUST be reviewed with your care team before use; this is a starting template, not medical advice.

exercises.name: Toe Taps
steps: Sit tall with heels resting on the floor.
Keeping your heels down, tap the toes of both feet up and down.
Find a light, steady rhythm for about 20 taps.
A nice way to wake up the legs.
exercises.seatedVariant: This exercise is done seated — no change needed.
exercises.safetyCue: Keep it light and easy at the ankles; no need to rush.

exercises.name: Knee Lift with Arm Reach
steps: Sit tall with feet flat.
Lift your right knee gently while raising your left arm overhead.
Lower both, then lift the left knee with the right arm.
Alternate slowly, about 8 times each side. A little coordination for body and mind.
exercises.seatedVariant: This exercise is done seated — no change needed.
exercises.safetyCue: Lift the knee only as high as is comfortable. Move at an easy pace.

exercises.name: Gentle Neck Side Tilts
steps: Sit tall with shoulders relaxed.
Slowly tilt your right ear toward your right shoulder until you feel a mild stretch.
Hold for a breath, return to center, then tilt left.
Repeat 4 times each side.
exercises.seatedVariant: This exercise is done seated — no change needed.
exercises.safetyCue: Let the head drop gently with gravity; never pull on your neck.

exercises.name: Chin Tucks
steps: Sit tall with eyes forward.
Gently draw your chin straight back, making a 'double chin,' without tilting your head.
Hold for 3 seconds, then relax.
Repeat about 8 times. Good for posture and neck comfort.
exercises.seatedVariant: This exercise is done seated — no change needed.
exercises.safetyCue: Keep it small and gentle; this should feel like a light tuck, not a strain.

exercises.name: Standing March at the Chair
steps: Stand behind a sturdy chair, holding the back with both hands.
Slowly march in place, lifting one knee at a time to a comfortable height.
Keep your posture tall and your hold light.
March gently for about 20 steps total.
exercises.seatedVariant: Seated: march in place while seated, lifting each knee in turn, about 20 steps.
exercises.safetyCue: Keep both hands on the chair. Lift knees only as high as feels steady.

exercises.name: Heel-to-Toe Stand
steps: Stand beside a counter or sturdy chair, holding on with one or both hands.
Place one foot directly in front of the other, heel nearly touching the back toes.
Hold this narrow stance for 10 seconds, staying tall.
Switch which foot is in front and repeat. Do 3 times each way.
exercises.seatedVariant: Seated: place one foot a step ahead of the other and hold, then switch, to practice the foot position safely.
exercises.safetyCue: Keep a firm hold on the support. Stop and widen your stance if you feel unsteady.

exercises.name: Seated Cat-Cow
steps: Sit tall with hands on your thighs.
Breathe in and gently arch your back, lifting your chest and looking slightly up.
Breathe out and round your back, tucking your chin toward your chest.
Flow slowly between the two for about 6 breaths.
exercises.seatedVariant: This exercise is done seated — no change needed.
exercises.safetyCue: Move gently with your breath; keep the range small and comfortable.

exercises.name: Seated Chest Opener
steps: Sit tall toward the front of the chair.
Bring your hands behind your head, elbows wide, or clasp them gently behind your back.
Gently open your elbows or lift your chest until you feel a light stretch across the front.
Hold for 15 seconds, breathing easily. Repeat twice.
exercises.seatedVariant: This exercise is done seated — no change needed.
exercises.safetyCue: A gentle opening across the chest is enough; don't force the shoulders.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Stretch
steps: Stand facing a wall or sturdy chair, hands resting on it.
Step one foot back, keeping that heel down and the back leg fairly straight.
Lean gently forward until you feel a mild stretch in the back calf.
Hold 15 to 20 seconds, then switch legs.
exercises.seatedVariant: Seated: loop a towel under the ball of one foot, straighten the leg, and gently pull the toes toward you for a calf stretch. Switch legs.
exercises.safetyCue: Keep hands on the support. A mild stretch only; avoid bouncing.

exercises.name: Seated Heel Slides
steps: Sit tall with both feet flat on the floor.
Slowly slide one heel back toward the chair, gently bending the knee as far as is comfortable.
Slide it forward again to straighten.
Do about 10 slow slides on each leg. Gentle movement for a stiff knee.
exercises.seatedVariant: This exercise is done seated — gentle and good for knee mobility.
exercises.safetyCue: Work within a comfortable, pain-free range for your knee. Never force the bend.
